notes: Half-maximal NO concentration for inhibition of effector T cell function (CD8 + Th). Rate law: H_NO = V_T.NO / (NO_50_Teff + V_T.NO) (MDSC_module.m:156); H_NO enters H_MDSC = 1 - (1-H_NO)*(1-H_ArgI_Teff), which multiplicatively suppresses T cell killing/proliferation/IFNg-secretion via (1 - H_MDSC) factors throughout the Teff/cytokine modules. Status: NO submodel target on disk. CSV prior median 1.5 nM (parameters_PDAC.m comment: 'Raised from 0.75 to move H_NO into graded range at baseline NO ~2.8 nM' — manual tuning, no primary citation). Joint NPE 20k posterior median 1.43 nM, sigma 0.7 (essentially prior). Posterior median V_T.NO = 10.5 nM → H_NO = 0.875 (saturated high in 21% of posterior sims at H>0.95). With H_ArgI_Teff also ≈ 0.82 (saturated), combined H_MDSC ≈ 0.97 — MDSC suppresses CD8 killing by ~97% at posterior median, blocking any path to observed cd8 density. Likely-too-low prior: classical MDSC literature reports NO suppression of T cell proliferation/cytokine production in the µM range (orders of magnitude above current 1.5 nM prior); maple to verify primary sources during extraction. Submodel structure: in vitro T cell suppression assay where activated CD8 (or splenocyte) proliferation / IFNγ-release is measured under titrated NO donor (DETA-NO, SNAP, GSNO, or co-culture with iNOS-induced macrophages). Forward model: standard Hill, T_response_fraction = T_baseline * (1 - V_max * NO/(NO_50_Teff + NO)); fit NO_50_Teff and V_max (T_baseline). Search guidance: look for foundational MDSC NO/T-cell papers (J Immunol, J Exp Med, Cancer Res, late 1990s through ~2010) that titrate an NO donor against CD8 proliferation, IL-2 production, or IFNγ; reviews of arginase/NO MDSC mechanisms typically cite the canonical dose-response studies. Critical: target is the T-cell-INTRINSIC NO EC50 from a clean dose-response, NOT in-tumor NO concentrations or iNOS expression levels. Avoid: studies that report only IC50 of iNOS-inhibitors (those measure inhibitor potency, not NO EC50); macrophage-functional readouts (NO has different EC50s on different effectors). Translation sigma: in vitro pure NO donor vs in-tumor mixed reactive nitrogen species (peroxynitrite, S-nitrosothiols) → moderate widening (σ_translate ~0.3 in log space). Critical experimental nuisances to capture in inputs: NO donor type (steady-state release rate matters), assay duration (T cell apoptosis at high NO confounds proliferation readouts beyond 24h), starting CD8 activation state. Acceptance: contraction_local ≥ 0.5 OR posterior median moves >100× from current prior median (1.5 nM → 100+ nM). Priority: HIGH — currently unanchored AND saturating; one of two top remaining structural tensions in the cd8/M1-M2 misfit cluster (notes/calibration/m2_m1_bottleneck_flux_analysis.md, 2026-05-05).

Half-maximal arginase-I concentration for inhibition of effector T cell function. Rate law: H_ArgI_Teff = V_T.ArgI / (ArgI_50_Teff + V_T.ArgI) (MDSC_module.m:157); enters H_MDSC = 1 - (1-H_NO)*(1-H_ArgI_Teff); also separately enters H_ArgI_Treg via ArgI_50_Treg parameter (different EC50, different reaction — not this target). Mechanism: MDSC-secreted Arg-I depletes extracellular L-arginine, causing T cell zeta-chain downregulation, anergy, and reduced proliferation. Status: NO submodel target on disk. CSV prior median 0.42 nM. parameters_PDAC.m Notes field cites Miret 2019 (PMID 30728077) as the original model source; that citation came with the existing model and has not been re-verified by this analysis — extraction should re-confirm the underlying primary data. Joint NPE 20k posterior median 0.391 nM, sigma 0.7 (essentially prior). Posterior median V_T.ArgI = 1.74 nM → H_ArgI_Teff = 0.815 (saturated high in 11% of posterior sims at H>0.95). With H_NO also saturated, combined H_MDSC dominates CD8 killing (see notes/calibration/m2_m1_bottleneck_flux_analysis.md). Likely-too-low prior: classical Arg-I T-cell-suppression literature reports EC50s for recombinant Arg-I in conditioned media at concentrations corresponding to roughly tens to hundreds of nM (1–10 µg/mL; Arg-I MW ~40 kDa) — orders of magnitude above current 0.42 nM prior. maple to verify primary sources during extraction. Note: published values are often reported as enzyme activity (U/mL) or arginine-depletion EC50, not arginase concentration; conversion requires the enzyme's specific activity. Submodel structure: T cell proliferation / IFNγ assay under titrated recombinant Arg-I or arginine-depleted media. Forward model: H_ArgI = ArgI/(ArgI_50_Teff + ArgI); T_response = T_baseline * (1 - V_max * H_ArgI). Fit ArgI_50_Teff and V_max. Alternative: arginine-titration assay where T cell function is plotted vs residual L-arginine; L-arg EC50 maps to ArgI EC50 via Michaelis kinetics if the L-Arg degradation rate constant is known. Search guidance: look for primary T-cell-Arg-I dose-response papers (Blood, J Immunol, Cancer Res, 2003–2010 era) reporting CD8 proliferation or IFNγ vs titrated recombinant Arg-I or vs L-arginine starting concentration; arginase MDSC reviews typically cite the canonical primary papers. Avoid: papers reporting only Arg-I expression levels in tumor tissue (these constrain V_T.ArgI, not the EC50); IDO-related immunometabolism reviews (different mechanism); MDSC-conditioned-medium experiments that don't titrate Arg-I quantitatively. Translation sigma: human peripheral T cells under recombinant Arg-I vs in-tumor PDAC TIL under MDSC-derived Arg-I → moderate widening (σ_translate ~0.3). Critical experimental nuisances to capture in inputs: arginine starting concentration in medium (RPMI is ~1.15 mM, suppression onset depends on absolute L-Arg concentration), Arg-I lot specific activity, assay duration. Acceptance: contraction_local ≥ 0.5 OR posterior median moves >50× from current prior median (0.42 → 25+ nM). Priority: HIGH — currently unanchored AND saturating in the cd8/M1-M2 cluster (paired with NO_50_Teff). RERUN: Search specifically for in vitro titrations of recombinant or pegylated arginase I (human or mouse) where the enzyme is added to T cell cultures at known concentrations (nM or U/mL) and T cell proliferation/cytokine production are measured as a graded function of ArgI dose. Prioritize papers that (1) report both ArgI activity units and mass concentration with a defined specific activity, (2) include time courses or endpoint measurements of extracellular L-arginine, and (3) use primary human or murine CD4/CD8 T cells activated via anti-CD3/anti-CD28. Useful search terms could include combinations of “recombinant human arginase I”, “peg-ArgI”, “dose-dependent suppression of T cell proliferation”, “arginase I units per mL”, “T cell cytokine production”, and “EC50” or “dose–response”. Also consider oncology or transplant immunology contexts where arginase-based therapeutics are used and dosing is reported quantitatively. RERUN: Search specifically for purified/recombinant human or mouse arginase I titrated onto activated primary T cells, PBMCs, CD3/CD28-stimulated CD4/CD8 T cells, or tumor-reactive T cells, with proliferation, CD3ζ, IL-2, IFNγ, or cytotoxicity readouts. Include terms such as: "recombinant arginase I T cell proliferation dose response", "purified arginase I CD3 zeta T cells", "arginase I ug/mL T cell suppression", "arginase activity U/mL T cell proliferation specific activity", "MDSC arginase I recombinant T cell IFN gamma", and look for papers reporting ArgI in µg/mL, nM, or U/mL with specific activity sufficient to convert to molar enzyme. RERUN: Search specifically for recombinant or purified arginase I/ARG1 dose-response experiments in activated primary T cells, CD8+ T cells, CD3+ T cells, splenocytes, or PBMCs with proliferation, IFN-gamma, IL-2, granzyme B, CD3zeta, or cytotoxicity readouts. Include terms such as: "recombinant arginase I" T cell proliferation dose response, "human arginase I" IFN-gamma T cells EC50, "ARG1" "ug/ml" "anti-CD3/CD28", "arginase activity mU/ml" T cell proliferation specific activity, and look for papers/supplemental data reporting multiple ARG1 mass concentrations or enough specific-activity information to convert activity units to molarity. If direct ArgI curves remain unavailable, consider redefining/calibrating the model target as residual extracellular L-arginine sensitivity rather than molar ArgI_50_Teff.
